arxiv-2012-13629.title: Continuous variable multimode quantum states via symmetric group velocity matching
arxiv-2012-13629.creator: V. Roman-Rodriguez, B. Brecht, S.Kaali, C. Silberhorn, N. Treps, E.Diamanti, V. Parigi
arxiv-2012-13629.description: Abstract Configurable and scalable continuous variable quantum networks for measurement-based quantum information protocols or multipartite quantum communication schemes can be obtained via parametric down conversion (PDC) in non-linear waveguides. In this work, we exploit symmetric group velocity matching (SGVM) to engineer the properties of the squeezed modes of the PDC.

arxiv-2202-07315.title: Using Social Media Images for Building Function Classification
arxiv-2202-07315.creator: Eike Jens Hoffmann, Karam Abdulahhad, Xiao Xiang Zhu
arxiv-2202-07315.description: Abstract Urban land use on a building instance level is crucial geo-information for many applications, yet difficult to obtain. An intuitive approach to close this gap is predicting building functions from ground level imagery. Social media image platforms contain billions of images, with a large variety of motifs including but not limited to street perspectives.

arxiv-2205-01567.title: Snowmass White Paper: Higher Spin Gravity and Higher Spin Symmetry
arxiv-2205-01567.creator: Xavier Bekaert, Nicolas Boulanger, Andrea Campoleoni, Marco Chiodaroli, Dario Francia, Maxim Grigoriev, Ergin Sezgin, Evgeny Skvortsov
arxiv-2205-01567.description: Abstract Higher Spin Gravity refers to extensions of gravity including at least one field of spin greater than two. These extensions are expected to provide manageable models of quantum gravity thanks to the infinite-dimensional (higher spin) gauge symmetry constraining them.

arxiv-2302-12561.title: Inducing Schemes with Finite Weighted Complexity
arxiv-2302-12561.creator: Jianyu Chen, Fang Wang, Hong-Kun Zhang
arxiv-2302-12561.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider a Borel measurable map of a compact metric space which admits an inducing scheme. Under the finite weighted complexity condition, we establish a thermodynamic formalism for a parameter family of potentials φ + t ​ ψ \varphi+t\psi in an interval containing t = 0 t=0 .

arxiv-2401-06814.title: Operad Structure of Poset Matrices This work was partially supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea (NRF) Grant funded by the Korean Government (MSIP)(2016R1A5A1008055). G.-S. Cheon was also partially supported by the NRF-2019R1A2C1007518.
arxiv-2401-06814.creator: Arnauld Mesinga Mwafise, Gi-Sang Cheon, Hong Joon Choi, Samuele Giraudo
arxiv-2401-06814.description: Abstract This paper examines operad structures derived from poset matrices by formulating a set of new construction rules for poset matrices. In this direction, eleven different partial composition operations will be introduced as the basis for the construction of poset matrices of any given size by extending the combinatorial setting of species of structures to poset matrices.

arxiv-2401-13250.title: Interferences effects in polarized nonlinear Breit-Wheeler process
arxiv-2401-13250.creator: Jing-Jing Jiang, Ya-Nan Dai, Kai-Hong Zhuang, Yunquan Gao, Suo Tang, Yue-Yue Chen
arxiv-2401-13250.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jing-Jing Jiang, Ya-Nan Dai, Kai-Hong Zhuang, Yunquan Gao, Suo Tang, Yue-Yue Chen. The creation of polarized electron-positron pairs by the nonlinear Breit-Wheeler process in short laser pulses is investigated using the Baier-Katkov semiclassical method beyond local-constant-field approximation (LCFA), which allows for identifying the interferences effects in the positron polarization.

arxiv-2409-17085.title: Parameter-efficient Bayesian Neural Networks for Uncertainty-aware Depth Estimation
arxiv-2409-17085.creator: Richard D. Paul Alessio Quercia Vincent Fortuin Katharina Nöh Hanno Scharr, [1mm] Forschungszentrum Jülich, Jülich, Germany
arxiv-2409-17085.description: Abstract State-of-the-art computer vision tasks, like monocular depth estimation (MDE), rely heavily on large, modern Transformer-based architectures. However, their application in safety-critical domains demands reliable predictive performance and uncertainty quantification. While Bayesian neural networks provide a conceptually simple approach to serve those requirements, they suffer from the high dimensionality of the parameter space.

arxiv-2412-00913.title: Garden city: A synthetic dataset and sandbox environment for analysis of pre-processing algorithms for GPS human mobility data
arxiv-2412-00913.creator: Thomas H. Li, Francisco Barreras
arxiv-2412-00913.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thomas H. Li, Francisco Barreras. Human mobility datasets have seen increasing adoption in the past decade, enabling diverse applications that leverage the high precision of measured trajectories relative to other human mobility datasets. However, there are concerns about whether the high sparsity in some commercial datasets can introduce errors due to lack of robustness in processing algorithms, which could compromise the validity of downstream results. The scarcity of “ground-truth” data makes it particularly challenging to evaluate and calibrate these algorithms.

arxiv-2501-14139.title: A Probabilistic WxChallenge Proposal Thanks: * Author’s previous affiliation and research location: Department of Geography and Meteorology, Valparaiso University, Valparaiso, IN 46383, U.S.A
arxiv-2501-14139.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . The national forecasting competition WxChallenge , brainchild of Brad Illston at the University of Oklahoma in 2005, has become a cherished institution played across the United States each year. Participants include students, faculty, alumni, and industry professionals.

arxiv-2502-06179.title: Actual Achieved Gain and Optimal Perceived Gain: Modeling Human Take-over Decisions Towards Automated Vehicles’ Suggestions
arxiv-2502-06179.creator: Shuning Zhang, Xin Yi, Shixuan Li, Chuye Hong, Gujun Chen, Jiarui Liu, Xueyang Wang, Yongquan Hu, Yuntao Wang, Hewu Li
arxiv-2502-06179.description: Abstract . Driver decision quality in take-overs is critical for effective human-Autonomous Driving System (ADS) collaboration. However, current research lacks detailed analysis of its variations. This paper introduces two metrics–Actual Achieved Gain (AAG) and Optimal Perceived Gain (OPG)–to assess decision quality, with OPG representing optimal decisions and AAG reflecting actual outcomes.

arxiv-2502-07107.title: A Framework for Supervised and Unsupervised Segmentation and Classification of Materials Microstructure Images
arxiv-2502-07107.creator: Kungang Zhang, Daniel W. Apley, Wei Chen, Wing K. Liu, L. Catherine Brinson
arxiv-2502-07107.description: Abstract Microstructure of materials is often characterized through image analysis to understand processing-structure-properties linkages. We propose a largely automated framework that integrates unsupervised and supervised learning methods to classify micrographs according to microstructure phase/class and, for multiphase microstructures, segments them into different homogeneous regions.

arxiv-2505-05292.title: QUIC-Exfil: Exploiting QUIC’s Server Preferred Address Feature to Perform Data Exfiltration Attacks
arxiv-2505-05292.creator: Thomas Grübl, Weijie Niu, Jan von der Assen, Burkhard Stiller
arxiv-2505-05292.description: Abstract . The QUIC protocol is now widely adopted by major tech companies and accounts for a significant fraction of today’s Internet traffic. QUIC’s multiplexing capabilities, encrypted headers, dynamic IP address changes, and encrypted parameter negotiations make the protocol not only more efficient, secure, and censorship-resistant, but also practically unmanageable by firewalls.

arxiv-2506-16376.title: Fast Converging Single Trace Quasi-local PMCHWT Equation for the Modelling of Composite Systems PubID: pubid:
arxiv-2506-16376.creator: Kristof Cools
arxiv-2506-16376.description: Abstract The PMCHWT integral equation enables the modelling of scattering of time-harmonic fields by penetrable, piecewise homogeneous, systems. They have been generalised to include the modelling of composite systems that may contain junctions, i.e. lines along which three or more materials meet.

arxiv-2602-00453.title: FedMOA: Federated GRPO for Personalized Reasoning LLMs under Heterogeneous Rewards
arxiv-2602-00453.creator: Ziyao Wang, Daeun Jung, Yexiao He, Guoheng Sun, Zheyu Shen, Myungjin Lee, Ang Li

arxiv-2602-09847.title: Stabilized Maximum-Likelihood Iterative Quantum Amplitude Estimation for Structural CVaR under Correlated Random Fields Journal: Journal of …..
arxiv-2602-09847.creator: Alireza Tabarraei
arxiv-2602-09847.description: Abstract Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) is a fundamental tail-risk measure in stochastic structural mechanics, yet its accurate evaluation under high-dimensional, spatially correlated material uncertainty remains computationally prohibitive for classical Monte Carlo methods. Leveraging bounded-expectation reformulations of CVaR compatible with quantum amplitude estimation, we develop a quantum-enhanced inference framework that casts CVaR evaluation as a statistically consistent, confidence-constrained maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation problem.

plos-pone-0009601.description: PLOS ONE research article. The pulmonary microcirculation is the chief regulatory site for resistance in the pulmonary circuit. Despite pulmonary microvascular dysfunction being implicated in the pathogenesis of several pulmonary vascular conditions, there are currently no techniques for the specific asses

pmc-10512581.title: Divergent roles of the Hippo pathway in the pathogenesis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: tissue homeostasis and fibrosis
pmc-10512581.creator: Ryusuke Kizawa, Jun Araya, Yu Fujita
pmc-10512581.description: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive aging-related lung disease with a poor prognosis. Despite extensive research, the cause of IPF remains largely unknown and treatment strategies are limited. Proposed mechanisms of the pathogenesis of IPF are a combination of excessive accumulation of the extracellular matrix and dysfunctional lung tissue regeneration.

pmc-11550630.title: Substantial medial para-meniscal cyst with a complex meniscal tear: A case report
pmc-11550630.creator: Muhammad Irfan Rajput, Muhammad Rafique, Muhammad Waqas Khan, Badaruddin Sahito, Nauman Hussain, Jemal Girma Mohammad
pmc-11550630.description: Introduction and importanceMeniscal cysts, while infrequent with a prevalence of 1 %–8 %, may result in considerable knee discomfort and functional limitations. The cysts are categorized according to their position in relation through the meniscus, labeled as either intrameniscal or parameniscal. Although parameniscal cysts are often small and asymptomatic, they may expand and become painful with time.

pmc-11700660.title: Multimodal deep learning approaches for precision oncology: a comprehensive review
pmc-11700660.creator: Huan Yang, Minglei Yang, Jiani Chen, Guocong Yao, Quan Zou, Linpei Jia
pmc-11700660.description: The burgeoning accumulation of large-scale biomedical data in oncology, alongside significant strides in deep learning (DL) technologies, has established multimodal DL (MDL) as a cornerstone of precision oncology. This review provides an overview of MDL applications in this field, based on an extensive literature survey. In total, 651 articles published before September 2024 are included.

pmc-12978442.title: Racial and ethnic disparities in fatal police shootings: Variation across U.S. states and the role of firearm ownership
pmc-12978442.creator: Roland Neil, Shawn Bushway, Terry L. Schell, Andrew R. Morral, Rosanna Smart
pmc-12978442.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fatal police shooting rates vary greatly across U.S. states, and states with higher firearm ownership rates tend to have higher rates of police shootings. Yet, despite well-documented national racial and ethnic disparities in fatal police shootings, prior research has not established how much these disparities vary across states, nor whether firearm ownership rates are associated with racial and ethnic disparities in police shootings.

pmc-13295559.title: Brilacidin’s Antifungal Mechanism: Insights from Lipid Membrane Models
pmc-13295559.creator: María Victoria López Nota Francisco, Milagro Mottola, Jessica Aye Valdivia Pérez, Julieta Tallone, Thaila Fernanda dos Reis, Gustavo H. Goldman, Candelaria Inés Cámara, Maria Laura Fanani
pmc-13295559.description: Background/Objectives: BRI is a synthetic arylamide polymer designed to mimic the electrostatic and amphiphilic features of defensin-type antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), although its molecular organization and activity have not been experimentally validated. This study presents the first integrated computational and experimental characterization of BRI to define the physicochemical basis of its AMP-like behavior and membrane interactions.

pmc-13326396.title: Patient and public involvement in pragmatic trials with older adults: a multi-methods study of researchers’ experiences
pmc-13326396.creator: Anne Spinewine, Perrine Evrard, Pascale Nevins, Tokandji Adda, Shelley Vanderhout, Karina Branje, Joanne Hutton, Maureen Smith, Monica Taljaard, Stuart G. Nicholls
pmc-13326396.description: BackgroundPatient and Public Involvement (PPI) in health research, including clinical trials, enhances research relevance and quality. However, data on PPI prevalence and characteristics in trials involving older adults remain scarce. We aimed to describe the prevalence and nature of PPI in trials with older adults and identify the main benefits and challenges associated with PPI in such trials.

pmc-13438372.title: Integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identify TRIP6 as a prognostic and EMT-associated biomarker in colorectal cancer
pmc-13438372.creator: Qiwei Cui, Xiaohong Gao, Xiaoqing Wu, Dongwei Zhang
pmc-13438372.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundColorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by profound molecular heterogeneity and complex tumor–microenvironment interactions, which contribute to invasion, metastasis, and variable clinical outcomes. More effective prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets are still needed.MethodsWe integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, multi-cohort bulk transcriptomic data, drug response prediction, and in vitro experiments to characterize malignant epithelial states in CRC and identify clinically relevant biomarkers and candidate therapeutics. Stemness, copy number variation, pathway activity, and cell–cell communication were analyzed at single-cell resolution.

pmc-13462410.title: Factors Associated with Successful Liberation from Continuous Renal Replacement Therapy in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Observational Study
pmc-13462410.creator: Satish Patel
pmc-13462410.description: IntroductionContinuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) supports hemodynamically unstable critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who cannot tolerate intermittent dialysis. Identifying predictors for successful CRRT discontinuation remains a challenge. Premature cessation may cause fluid and electrolyte imbalance, while delayed withdrawal increases morbidity and hospital stay.

pmc-13470398.title: Beyond a waste product: lactate as a master metabolite dictating anti-tumor T-cell fate
pmc-13470398.creator: Xiangyu Dai, Jingjia Chang, Siyue Wang, Lutterodt Bentum-Ennin, Jian Zhou, Xiaomin Zuo, Wanglai Hu

pmc-13657553.title: Delayed-onset central neurotoxic syndrome with predominant cerebellar dysfunction following combined chlorpyrifos and cypermethrin poisoning: a case report
pmc-13657553.creator: Sobin Pant, Dibij Adhikari, Anush Acharya, Sachet Subedi, Jayaram Lamichhane, Bikram Prasad Gajurel
pmc-13657553.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Organophosphate (OP) poisoning typically manifests in three phases: the acute cholinergic crisis, the intermediate syndrome, and OP-induced delayed neuropathy (OPIDN). Delayed central nervous system sequelae with predominant cerebellar dysfunction are exceptionally rare and poorly characterized. We report the case of a woman in her early thirties with a history of chronic alcohol use who ingested a commercial insecticide containing chlorpyrifos (50%) and cypermethrin (2%).

uslaw-usc-t18-s1911.title: 18 U.S.C. § 1911 — Receiver mismanaging property
uslaw-usc-t18-s1911.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s1911.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 93 (Public Officers And Employees). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever, being a receiver, trustee, or manager in possession of any property in any cause pending in any court of the United States, willfully fails to manage and operate such property according to the requirements of the valid laws.
